note: updateItem(afterAway?: boolean): 'if (!afterAway) { <probabilistic review-nudge skip> }' is a real caller-facing mode - called with true only from the 5-minutes-back-from-away window handler, vs the normal unconditional poll path.

_refresh(clear: boolean): 'if (clear) { this._index.clear() }' before rebuilding is a genuine full-rebuild vs incremental-merge branch, though the only current call site always passes false - clear is dead-in-practice today, not merely forwarded.
didChange(uri, deleted): 'if (deleted) { graph.delete(...) } else { node.isSynced = false }' is a textbook Remove Flag Argument target - a public API method that could split into didDelete/didModify.
produceOne(..., upload: boolean): 'if (!upload) { return undefined }' skips the upload step after building - dry-run vs publish caller-facing mode.

findNodeModulesFiles(location, inNodeModules, result): the sole external call site passes false; every other appearance is the function threading its own computed value (inNodeModules || (entry === 'node_modules')) through recursive self-calls - traversal-accumulator state, not a caller-selected behavior mode.
main(force: boolean): 'if (!force) { <frozen-quality check, may skip release> }' - force comes straight from a CLI arg (process.argv), the classic --force-flag call-site confusion Fowler describes.
